claims.text: An access policy for an agent is only as real as its worst row, the one whose enforcement is that the agent has been told.
claims.quote: An access policy for an agent is only as real as its worst row.

claims.text: The account, not the session, is the blast radius, because every session an agent opens through a connector runs as the account that authorised it.
claims.quote: Every session an agent opens through a connector runs as the account that authorised it

claims.text: Each agent identity runs on a dedicated Google Workspace account, a seat on a Claude Team plan and a GitHub account of its own, so nothing the agent does runs as the owner.
claims.quote: Nothing the agent does runs as me.

claims.text: A Google Workspace seat per agent costs about 7 pounds a month.
claims.quote: A Workspace seat per agent is £7 a month.

claims.text: Six roles share the two identities, the agent for RiskMandate and the agent for the owner's own domain, split by what each is allowed to touch.
claims.quote: Six roles share those two identities, and the split follows what each one is allowed to touch

claims.text: A dedicated account puts each agent in its own organisational unit, and Google Workspace applies its Gmail compliance rules per unit, so they become per-agent enforcement.
claims.quote: Google Workspace applies its Gmail compliance rules per unit.

claims.text: Three Workspace settings matter, all applied per unit: restrict delivery, attachment compliance and scope limits on third-party apps.
claims.quote: Three settings turned out to matter, all under Apps, Google Workspace, Gmail, Compliance in the Admin console

claims.text: With the Claude GitHub App installed per repository or a fine-grained token, the site editor's GitHub account sees the website repository and nothing else.
claims.quote: The site editor's account sees the website repository and nothing else.

claims.text: The reader's rule of never sending became never reply unless the message came from the owner, and it changed on the first scheduled run.
claims.quote: never reply, unless the message came from me, in which case act on it

claims.text: Policies get written from the workflow one exception at a time, and the list of exceptions is the policy, complete only after the workflow has run for a while.
claims.quote: this is how policies actually get written: from the workflow, one exception at a time

claims.text: The reply-to-me exception is an authentication problem, not a permissions one, and needs a signature check against the append-lane registry with the owner's key added.
claims.quote: Anyone can put my address in a From header.

claims.text: On 27 September an agent working in Cowork found that create_draft and update_draft accept an attachments array and proved it with a signed PDF that arrived intact.
claims.quote: On 27 September an agent working in Cowork needed to send a signed letter and found the way.

claims.text: The agent shrank a 1.4 MB scanned PDF to 17 KB before base64-encoding it into the draft.
claims.quote: It shrank a 1.4 MB scanned PDF to 17 KB

claims.text: Anthropic's two documentation pages disagree: one says the Gmail connector only reads and searches, the other says it can send, reply and forward.
claims.quote: the vendor's documentation disagrees with itself

claims.text: The Gmail API puts drafting and sending in the same scope, so the admin's scope limit cannot express the rule drafts only.
claims.quote: There is no scope that allows drafts and forbids sending.

claims.text: In this setup the Cowork agent has no GitHub connector and cannot open the repository, while the Claude Code agent on the same seat edits the site.
claims.quote: The Cowork agent, in this setup, has no GitHub connector and cannot open the repository at all

claims.text: On a Team plan an Owner enables or disables a connector for the whole organisation; per-tool control to block an action exists only on the Enterprise plan.
claims.quote: On a Team plan an Owner enables or disables a connector for the whole organisation

claims.text: The rows that touch identity, code and vaults are enforced by accounts, repositories and keys; the rows that touch mail are admin rules and approvals; two rows are only told.
claims.quote: The rows that touch identity, code and vaults are enforced, because accounts, repositories and keys are boundaries the platform or the mathematics maintains.

claims.text: The row acts outside its role is shared by every agent policy in the world and no setting anywhere enforces it.
claims.quote: is the row every agent policy in the world shares, and no setting anywhere enforces it

claims.text: Write the policy as a table with an enforcement column, fill it honestly, and have an agent try the things the policy assumes it cannot do before writing it.
claims.quote: Have an agent try the things the policy assumes it cannot do.

claims.text: The owner's own key is not yet in the signature registry, so the reader's exception is still enforced by instruction.
claims.quote: my own key in that registry, so the reader's exception is still enforced by instruction

claims.text: The policy table is the honest state of a real setup on 29 September 2026, published with its two told rows rather than pretending they are something else.
claims.quote: The policy table above is the honest state of a real setup on 29 September 2026

claims.text: The attachment finding is not a bypass: the agent used a documented field of a documented call, and the policy was wrong about capability.
claims.quote: It is not a bypass. The agent used a documented field of a documented call.

claims.text: The connector twin argument holds: replay what an agent can do before writing down what it may do.
claims.quote: before you write down what an agent may do, replay what it can do

claims.text: nhi.sgit.ai's August scoring of shared drives found that everything runs on your identity, segregation is the only granularity and nothing supports per-agent keys.
claims.quote: the only granularity is segregation rather than scoping, and nothing supports per-agent keys

claims.text: Putting the reader in a unit whose delivery is restricted to the owner's domain bounds the failure of a spoofed instruction, because the reply can only reach the owner.
claims.quote: It makes the worst row bounded.

claims.text: No broker yet exists that would make drafts only a block rather than a prompt on a Team plan, and there is no way to enforce acts outside its role.
claims.quote: a broker that would let
